newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: British and Danish kidnap victims freed in Colombia. [CORRECTED 00:30 GMT 17/9]
newsitem.headline: British and Danish kidnap victims freed in Colombia. [CORRECTED 00:30 GMT 17/9]

text.p: (Corrects inaccurate government information on the German victim Ulrich Schultz.)
A Briton and a Dane were set free in northwest Colombia over the weekend, seven months after being seized by leftist guerrillas, authorities said on Monday.
Police and diplomatic sources said the two were released by National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels on Saturday on the outskirts of Medellin, the capital of northwestern Antioquia province.
The Briton, Philip Halden, flew home on Sunday after his seven-month ordeal, a British embassy source said.
A confusing statement released earlier on Monday by Antioquia Gov. Alvaro Uribe Velez suggested that Halden and Karl Heinz of Denmark had been kidnapped together with Ulrich Shultz of Germany.
A German embassy spokesman said Shultz had been kidnapped separately, however, and was freed "several months ago" under circumstances that had nothing to do with Halden and Heinz.

Press spokesmen for Uribe Velez were unable to explain the confusion or the governor's claim that the German government, or a German company which he did not identify, had somehow entered into a "pact with guerrillas" by arranging a ransom payment of more than $2 million to secure the release of foreign kidnap victims in Antioquia.
Halden and Heinz had been working as consultants for cement manufacturer Cementos Rio Claro when they were abducted by ELN rebels in a rural area of Antioquia in early February.
Spokesmen for Rio Claro could not be reached for comment on the case.
Colombia has one of the highest kidnapping rates in the world and roughly half of all the abductions are believed to be the work of leftist guerrillas.
